12 March 2026

Monetary policy in a changing economy

Speaker: Christine Lagarde

Introduction

Ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon. It is a pleasure to welcome you to Frankfurt today.

Economic outlook

The euro area economy is expected to continue to expand at a moderate pace.

Real GDP is projected to grow by 1.2% in 2026 and by 1.4% in 2027.

Inflation

Headline inflation is projected to average 2.4% in 2025, 2.0% in 2026 and 1.9% in 2027.

Core inflation is projected to average 2.3% in June 2026.

Inflation expectations remained well anchored.

Labour market

The unemployment rate is projected to average 6.2% in 2026.

Wage growth is projected to average 3.8% in 2026.

Financial stability

Financial conditions remained tight and monetary policy transmission continued to function smoothly.

Bank lending rates are estimated to have reached 4.2% in June 2026.

Monetary policy

The Governing Council decided to keep its key interest rates unchanged.

The Council stands ready to adjust all of its instruments within its mandate, for as long as necessary.

Risks

Risks to economic growth were broadly balanced.

Upside risks to inflation remained, mainly reflecting energy and food prices.

Closing remarks

Thank you for your attention.

European Central Bank, 2026
